answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once, which means an operator running a synchronised farm is punished proportionally to the size of the group he synchronised. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The prism is the collateral at risk, the falcon the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the copper the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many falcon groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the prism into smaller, individually useless stakes.
